clue.text: Bar restricts sandwiches

parts.note: bar in the sense of except, as in 'all bar one'
ties means binds or restricts

explanation.surface: A pub's rules limit what sandwiches may be served at the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub but is the word for except.
explanation.definitionFit: Butty is a northern English informal word for a sandwich, especially a filled roll of chips or bacon.

clue.text: Next to see bid going awry

indicators.note: going awry means going wrong, so the preceding words come out in a muddled order

parts.note: every letter of both words is used

explanation.surface: At an auction a neighbour watches an offer go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside is a preposition meaning alongside or at the side of, the same as next to.

clue.text: Tour's leader conducted groups around quiet parts of church

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the groups word wraps the quiet one
a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter of that word counts

parts.note: the first letter of this word
ran as in managed or conducted a business
sets are groups or collections
p is piano, the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A tour guide leads groups quietly round a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: Transepts are the arms of a cross-shaped church lying across the nave, so they are parts of it.

clue.text: Illegally acquired title long abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned can mean wild and unrestrained, so the letters before it run loose

parts.note: every letter of both words is used

explanation.surface: An aristocratic title gained unlawfully has long since been given up.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-gotten describes gains obtained by dishonest or unlawful means.

clue.text: Police officer's great purpose securing result

parts.note: super means excellent or great

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the purpose word clasps the result inside it

parts.note: intent means aim or purpose
an end is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: A police officer's grand aim is to get a result.
explanation.walkthrough: The result word goes inside the purpose word after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A superintendent is a senior British police rank, above chief inspector.

clue.text: Instrument of Ethiopian origin

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A musical instrument said to come from Ethiopia.
explanation.definitionFit: The piano is a keyboard musical instrument with hammers striking strings.

clue.text: Incorrect, first off, under pressure to make projection

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter is removed from the word before it
in a down answer, under places this part below the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
wrong means incorrect

explanation.surface: A mistake made under pressure produces a projection.
explanation.definitionFit: A prong is a pointed part sticking out from a fork or tool, a kind of projection.

clue.text: Cooker fashionable once more

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of heavy range cooker
in means in fashion

explanation.surface: An old-style kitchen range is trendy again.
explanation.definitionFit: Again is an adverb meaning another time, which is exactly once more.

clue.text: Plain vase set aside

parts.note: overt means open and plain to see
an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: An unadorned vase has been put to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set aside' means annul, as a higher court does to a verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: To overturn a decision or ruling is to reverse or annul it, which is what set aside means legally.

clue.text: Engineer sees all in tests for alloy resisting corrosion

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or contrive, so the letters that follow are built into something new

parts.note: every letter of these four words is used

explanation.surface: An engineer oversees every trial of a rust-proof metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stainless steel contains chromium, which makes it an alloy that does not rust or tarnish.

clue.text: Stand in market and play for time

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a trader's booth or table

explanation.surface: A market trader dawdles to avoid making a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a market trader's booth and a verb for using delaying tactics.

clue.text: Peculiar part about period custom

indicators.note: something peculiar is odd or out of shape, so the next word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled
on means concerning or about
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An odd bit of a historical period's customs.
explanation.walkthrough: Custom here is the business a shop gets from its regular buyers.
explanation.definitionFit: Patronage is the regular trade a customer brings to a shop, which is also called custom.

clue.text: Holding forth with jibe about search linked to offence

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jibe goes round what follows

parts.note: a dig is a cutting remark
to scour is to search thoroughly
a sin is a moral offence

explanation.surface: Someone lecturing at length, mocking an investigation into a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The jibe word is split around the search and offence words joined together.
explanation.definitionFit: Discoursing means speaking at length on a subject, which is what holding forth describes.

clue.text: Final trap

definitions.meaning: first meaning: after all deductions, as in the end result
second meaning: a mesh for catching fish or animals

explanation.walkthrough: 'Final trap' reads as a last snare; the words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Net describes a figure after deductions, the final amount, and is also a mesh used to catch creatures.

clue.text: Rough earth behind shelter covered with light, shiny material

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the jumbled word is placed second, following the wrapped shelter
covered with means wrapped by, so the shelter sits inside the light word

parts.note: pale means light in colour
a tent is a canvas shelter

indicators.note: rough means crude or unformed, so the next word's letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: Campers pitch a shelter on rough ground in pale light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' places the jumbled earth after the light word holding the shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent leather is leather given a hard glossy lacquered finish, used for shoes and bags.

clue.text: Dubious writings, variable in approach, confused

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: y is a standard algebraic variable
taken as written

explanation.surface: Questionable texts whose approach varies and muddles the reader.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are writings of doubtful authorship or authenticity, especially books outside the biblical canon.

clue.text: Crossing last bits of slippery marsh, turned up with fuel for boat

indicators.note: in a down answer, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a ford is a shallow river crossing

indicators.note: last bits means the final letter of each word that follows

parts.note: the last letter of each of these two words
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A boat crossing a slippery marsh, overturned and in need of fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: The crossing and the two final letters together are reversed, then the fuel is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrofoil is a boat whose hull is lifted clear of the water on underwater wings at speed.

clue.text: Put away promising reforms? Not good

indicators.note: reforms means forms anew, so the letters are reshaped into another word
not good means the letter standing for good must be dropped

parts.note: taken as written; G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: Is locking people up a hopeful kind of reform? Apparently not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reforms' fits the penal surface but is the anagram signal; 'put away' is slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone away is informal for sending them to prison, so it means to jail or lock up.

clue.text: Modern studios sadly not appreciated

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the two words before it are rearranged

parts.note: every letter of both words is used

explanation.surface: Contemporary artists' workshops are sadly undervalued.
explanation.definitionFit: To be misunderstood is to have one's worth or intentions wrongly judged, so not properly valued.

clue.text: Agreement when posted

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
posted means sent by mail

explanation.surface: A consent given at the moment a letter is mailed.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is formal approval or consent, which is a form of agreement.

clue.text: Witty in speech? It's the whisky

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the clue's synonym

parts.note: wry means drily humorous

explanation.surface: Someone asks which whisky makes a person amusing in conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a whisky distilled mainly from rye grain, popular in North America.

clue.text: Joint venture's ending with large yield

indicators.note: ending means only the final letter of that word is taken

parts.note: the last letter of this word
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
to bow is to give way or yield

explanation.surface: A shared business project finishes with a big return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint venture' reads as a business phrase, but the definition is just 'Joint'.
explanation.definitionFit: The elbow is the hinge joint between the upper arm and forearm.

clue.text: Busy river tour is arranged

parts.note: the Indus is a great river of Pakistan

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the words before it are reordered

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A packed schedule as a river cruise is organised.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrious means hard-working and always occupied, which matches busy as a description of a person.

clue.text: Bury regular items in tip, not near

indicators.note: regular items means letters taken at even intervals from the words that follow

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and so on letters of these words

explanation.surface: Dispose of things at the rubbish dump rather than close by.
explanation.walkthrough: A tip is a British rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place a body in a grave, which is to bury it.

clue.text: Advance point of view, being content

parts.note: a sub is an advance on wages
a stance is an attitude or position

explanation.surface: Someone advances an opinion while feeling satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like the adjective for happy but is the noun for what something contains; a sub is a British word for an advance on pay.
explanation.definitionFit: The substance of a speech or book is its essential matter, that is its content as a noun.

clue.text: Investigate pair with honour

parts.note: PR is the standard abbreviation for pair
the OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: Look into two people who have received a decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe is to examine or inquire into something closely and searchingly.

clue.text: More recent tune we recognise partly

indicators.note: partly means only a portion of the preceding words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters span the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A listener half-recognises a freshly released song.
explanation.definitionFit: Newer is the comparative of new, meaning more recently made or arrived.

clue.text: Field left in wild condition for advertisement?

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, a crossword favourite

indicators.note: something in a wild condition is untamed and disordered, so the letters before it are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, to be jumbled

explanation.surface: A meadow left to grow wild is offered up as a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is an example: not every flyer is an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a printed sheet handed out, often to promote or advertise something.
